html:
Eloy Alfaro was the leader of the Liberal Revolution of 1895 in Ecuador and president from 1895 to 1901 and 1906 to 1911. He separated Church and state and built the railway from Guayaquil to Quito.

A merchant from the coast, he fought conservative governments for decades and took power after a rising in Guayaquil on 5 June 1895. He brought in secular schools, civil marriage and divorce, took over Church lands, and opened education to women. His railway, finished in 1908, climbed the Andes to Quito and joined the coast and the highlands for the first time.

After he fell from power, he returned in 1912 during a civil war, was jailed in Quito, and was dragged out by a mob, killed and burned. He is honoured as Ecuador's great reformer, the opposite pole to García Moreno in the history of Ecuador.
sum: Eloy Alfaro was the leader of the Liberal Revolution of 1895 in Ecuador and president from 1895 to 1901 and 1906 to 1911. He separated Church and state and built the railway from Guayaquil to Quito.
